item.title: Sabbatical Candidates Kickstart Their Campaigns at Dining Hall Hustings
item.description: On Monday, February 16th, the first major hustings event of the election cycle took place on the steps of the Dining Hall. After a few words from Bailey Armstrong, Head of the Electoral Commission, all 20 candidates gave a two-minute speech each. UT Editor Speaking first, Harper Alderson gave her speech. item.title: Memorandum
item.description: Memorandum is a retrospective showcase that is currently on view at the Olivier Cornet Gallery and is running until February 28th. The premise of this show is to display the pinnacle works of each exhibition that has been housed in this space during 2025, creating an exhibition that encapsulates the artworks of 15 artists from across the island. item.title: Five of the Best Eats Within Five Minutes of Campus
item.description: A long day of classes or hours in the library calls for a much-needed study break at one of the many delicious spots around campus. Luckily, Trinity is right in the city centre, surrounded by coffee shops, cafes, fast food spots, and sit-down restaurants to match whatever mood you’re in. item.title: An Examination Of Trinity’s Leadership and Bureaucracy
item.description: It’s likely that almost every Trinity student has crashed out from the frustration of not being able to get their problems solved due to the College’s disorganised bureaucratic system. item.title: Comhairle Hustings Takes Place Prior to Comhairle 5
item.description: The Comhairle Hustings took place on February 17th, at 6pm in the Edmund Burke Theatre. item.title: Comhairle 5: What You Missed
item.description: Comhairle 5 took place promptly after the Trinity College Dublin Students’ Union (TCDSU/AMLCT) Election Hustings, in the Edmund Burke Theatre, at 7.41pm, on Tuesday, February 17th. After the minutes were approved, the Officers gave their reports. Grace McNally, TCDSU President, was the first to give her report. She expressed her excitement about the first meeting of the campaign committee, as well as the sexual violence task force being formed. Buster Whaley, the Education Officer, spoke second.
